name: Example: Determining Intervals of Increasing or Decreasing Displacement
problem: The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t) = t^4 - 32t$, where $t \geq 0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$
worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of decreasing $x,$ then its velocity is negative. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-32t) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-32\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x$, we solve the inequality $v(t) <    0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & <0 \\ 4{t}^{3}-32 & <0 \\ 4{t}^{3} & <32 \\ {t}^{3} & <8 \\ t & <2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of decreasing $x$ is $t\in\left[ 0, 2\right).$
